idiom_name: hand-written wrapper class implementing the component interface; Function<C,C>/UnaryOperator<T> for composition
implementation_notes: Java has the composition half - java.util.function.Function and UnaryOperator<T> are documented functional interfaces with identity/andThen/compose - but no component type, so the enhancer is hand-written: either a Function<Component,Component> applied where components are factories, or a wrapper class that implements the same interface as the wrapped component and delegates to it, which is what the pattern becomes once a component is an interface. The function form fits enhancers that produce a new component instance from a factory; the wrapper class is required whenever the framework demands a concrete type (a view subclass, a component model, a filter in a servlet-style chain).
pitfalls: Type erasure: a generic enhancer such as Function<C,C> loses the wrapped type's type parameters, so typed props cannot be preserved without unchecked casts or a keyed type token.
Anonymous and lambda wrappers are invisible to reflection-based frameworks (component scanning, DI, serialization): use a named class when the container must see the component type.
Composition order is easy to invert: andThen/compose read right-to-left while a hand-written wrapper chain reads inside-out, so the effective order of two enhancers differs between the two styles.
